answer.label: Not Bob Marley — a modern misattribution
answer.sourceLine: This line is pinned to Bob Marley all over the internet, but it appears in none of his songs, interviews or documented writing, and researchers cannot find any use of it before roughly 2001 — two decades after his death in 1981. Wikiquote files it among his unsourced quotes with the note “He never said this” ↗. The true author is unknown.

source.excerpt: Truth is, everybody is going to hurt you; you just gotta find the ones worth suffering for.
trail: Wikiquote lists the line among Marley’s unsourced quotes, flagged “He never said this and I don’t know where this started” ↗.
The Houston Press traced the wording and found no use of it before 2001 ↗, two decades after Marley died in 1981.
The quote does not appear in the sourced section of Marley’s Wikiquote page ↗ or in his lyrics and interviews.
source.excerptNote: Circulated in many near-identical variants (“The truth is, everyone is going to hurt you…”), a hallmark of a line passed hand-to-hand online rather than quoted from a fixed text.

author.name: Bob Marley
author.heading: About the credited name
author.bio: Bob Marley was a Jamaican singer, songwriter and Rastafari icon who brought reggae to a global audience with Bob Marley and the Wailers. His lyrics on love, faith and liberation made him one of the 20th century’s most quoted musicians — which is exactly why feel-good lines he never wrote, like this one, so easily attach to his name.

misattribution.heading: Why this one is a fake
misattribution.intro: Bob Marley is one of the internet’s biggest magnets for invented inspirational quotes, and this is a textbook case: hugely popular, endlessly shared, and completely without a source.

items.why: It appears in no Marley song, interview or writing, and Wikiquote files it under unsourced quotes with the note “He never said this” ↗.
The Houston Press could find no use of the line before 2001 ↗ — twenty years after Marley’s death in 1981.

misattribution.truthLine: No documented author exists for this exact wording; despite millions of Marley-branded shares, no one has produced a primary source ↗.

context.heading: Why it sticks to Marley
lead: Marley’s public image — love, endurance, spiritual calm — makes almost any warm aphorism feel plausible in his voice, so lines with no origin drift toward his name and stay there. The quote even circulates in several slightly different wordings, which is the signature of a saying passed around online rather than quoted from a fixed song or text.

That the sentiment is appealing doesn’t make it his. Until someone produces a recording, interview or manuscript, the honest verdict is that Bob Marley did not say this — and its real author is unknown.
context.pull: Widely shared, deeply Marley-flavored, and completely unsourced.
